subject: Initial: SLA uplift & monthly credit cap for Olive Systems
messages:
From: Marco Ruiz <marco@olive-sys.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@olive-sys.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask ahead of POC kickoff

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning — team was impressed with the latency characteristics on the 8k context demos. Before we start the POC next week, procurement asked us to confirm a couple of SLA items so we can sign a short SOW quickly:

1) Uptime: your standard template lists 99.95% for hosted inference. Given our latency-sensitive consumer workflow, we need 99.985% for the first 90 days of the POC. Is that something Redwood can temporarily commit to, or do you prefer a higher credit for reduced uptime?

2) Monthly credit cap: our CFO wants an explicit cap on monthly service credits. If uptime drops below 99.985% during the POC, we expect credits to accrue, but we need to ensure the cap won’t exceed 20% of the monthly invoice.

3) Maintenance windows: can you confirm planned maintenance windows and whether they’re excluded from uptime calculations?

We don’t want to renegotiate your enterprise SLA long-term — just trying to get a short-term carve-in for the POC. If needed we can sign a limited amendment or MSA addendum.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — our kickoff is Monday.

Best,
Marco
Head of Platform, Olive Systems
[attachment: PO-terms.pdf (pdf)]
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marco Ruiz <marco@olive-sys.com>
Cc: procurement@olive-sys.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask ahead of POC kickoff

Hi Marco — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: we can propose a temporary uplift for the POC and we can set a cap on credits. I’ll loop in Legal & Solutions to propose language and numbers.

Couple notes for context:
- 99.985% is a tighter target than our standard hosted SLA; operationally we can run the POC on a reserved pool to get closer to that threshold. That will impact price slightly (I’ll detail in the follow-up).
- By default maintenance windows are excluded if we provide notice, but we can document a restricted maintenance carveout for the POC.

I’ll coordinate a short redline we can attach to the SOW this afternoon.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SLA ask ahead of POC kickoff — need recommended language

Laura / Connor — forwarding Marco’s note (below). Olive wants a temporary POC commitment to 99.985% for 90 days and a hard monthly credit cap at 20% of invoice. Can Legal confirm we’re comfortable with a time-limited uplift and advise on the credit calculation and cap?

Specific asks:
- Draft a 90-day amendment (POC Uplift Addendum) that pins uptime at 99.985% and defines credits as percentage-of-monthly-invoice (standard calculation but capped at 20%).
- Confirm whether we should require the POC to run on Reserved Dedicated capacity (recommendation: yes; note price delta).
- Maintenance carveout language — suggest we limit maintenance exclusions to emergency fixes only during the POC, else it counts toward uptime.

Marco expects a response before end of day so they can finalize the kickoff. Happy to call if easier.

Thanks,
Karthik
(on behalf of Olive Systems deal OLV-2026-091)
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 15:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA ask ahead of POC kickoff — need recommended language

Karthik — thanks for the heads up. Draft proposal below; I’ve attached an annotated redline (SLA_redline_OliveSystems_v1.pdf) and a simple monthly-credit calculator (monthly-credit-matrix.xlsx). Key points: 

1) Time-limited uplift: Redwood will grant a 90-day POC uptime uplift to 99.985% provided the POC is deployed on a Dedicated Reserved pool and Olive commits to the agreed reserved spend for the POC period. Language: "Redwood will, for a period of ninety (90) days following commencement of the POC, measure Availability against a 99.985% threshold ("POC Availability")."

2) Credit calculation: keep standard remedy (pro-rata monthly credit based on minutes of degraded availability) but add a hard cap equal to 20% of the monthly invoice for the POC term. Language: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Customer's total monetary credits for any month during the POC Term shall not exceed twenty percent (20%) of the Monthly Fees paid or payable for that month."

3) Maintenance carveout: include a defined maintenance window list and require >=72 hours' notice for any non-emergency maintenance during the POC; emergency maintenance still excluded with exception reporting.

4) Escalation / monitoring: require Redwood to provide an ops contact and a weekly health report during POC.

Operational caveats to flag with the customer: Dedicated pools reduce cross-tenant noise but do not make us immune to regional infra events. We should surface that to set expectations and ensure Olive’s reliability teams are aligned.

If that looks good I’ll send Marco a redlined addendum and ask Procurement to sign the short MSA addendum.

—Laura Bennett
VP, Legal & Contracts, Redwood Inference
[attachment: SLA_redline_OliveSystems_v1.pdf (pdf)]
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marco Ruiz <marco@olive-sys.com>
Cc: procurement@olive-sys.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask ahead of POC kickoff — Redwood POC addendum proposal

Marco — attaching the POC addendum we discussed (see SLA_redline_OliveSystems_v1.pdf) and a one-tab credit matrix for transparency. Summary of what we propose for the POC: 

- POC term: 90 days from kickoff (start date to be confirmed in SOW).
- Uptime target: 99.985% for POC term.
- Credits: standard pro-rata monthly credit formula, capped at 20% of the monthly invoice for any month in the POC term.
- Deployment: POC runs on a Dedicated Reserved pool (small price adjustment; see note below).
- Maintenance: non-emergency maintenance requires 72-hour notice and will be excluded from Availability calculations when properly notified; emergency maintenance will be excluded but reported.
- Reporting: weekly ops health report + named ops contact during POC.

If Olive is comfortable with the above we can attach the addendum to the SOW and get Procurement to countersign. Connor — ops contact is ready to stand up the reserved pool once we have the signed addendum.

Two quick items for transparency: moving the POC to reserved capacity increases monthly cost roughly 18% versus shared hosted; we can absorb some of that into a one-time credit if that helps close. Also, if the POC extends beyond 90 days the uplift will be subject to re-evaluation.

Would you prefer we circulate the PDF or jump on a 15-min call to close?

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
